choiceInstructions: Choose the actor's next action in a turn-based tactical battle using `gameplay` for rules and only observed or remembered facts in the state. Follow `commander_prompt` for faction priorities and `entity_prompt` for this entity's role; commander priorities win explicit conflicts. When no specific order applies, use `faction_goal`. AP means action points: actor.ap is the remaining budget, each action spends its listed cost. An action marked ends_activation ends the actor's activation and forfeits any remaining AP; otherwise a new decision follows if AP remains. HP means health points. capability_ref refers to the shared capabilities dictionary. The game handles pathfinding; north is -z, east +x, south +z and west -x. Resolve names in orders against actor.name and entities[].name. Historical sightings and radar pings are not visible attack targets. Consider objectives, cover, hazards, survival and friendly fire. Select only an offered option; choosing a group does not spend AP or execute an action.

choiceTasks.action-type: Choose the best specific action to take next. Each available weapon, usable item, and other ability is listed separately for this actor. Choose the weapon or item now; its target or destination will be selected in a follow-up containing ONLY that action.
choiceTasks.action-group: The action type has been chosen. Choose a region or target group within that type; a subsequent request will choose the concrete action.
choiceTasks.movement-target: Which destination or direction should actor move toward to follow its orders? Match entity names and metadata, including shared capabilities. Choose a known entity, objective, extraction zone, the map edge exit when offered, compass direction or retreat. The game finds a legal route to a free tile beside an entity, toward an objective, into the extraction zone, or in that direction. Reaching extraction does not board the actor; a TDF unit must choose Extract once inside. A follow-up decides how much of the one-AP route to use. Questions spend no AP.
choiceTasks.action: The specific action, including its weapon or item, has been chosen. Choose the best target or destination from ONLY the offered options for that action.

actionTypeSuffix: Read each option's instructions and capability before choosing.
distanceInstructions: How much of the available movement should the actor use to follow its orders? Follow commander_prompt over conflicting entity_prompt; otherwise use faction_goal. The movement destination has already been selected in selected_movement. Consider all actor and entity metadata; capability_ref points to shared capabilities. Rate the desired movement extent using the ordered levels. Any move costs exactly 1 AP, even a short move; unused movement points are lost. A shorter move does not preserve AP. The game divides the score by 4, scales the proposed route's movement-point cost, and rounds up to the next legal nonzero stopping point that still follows the selected intent, capped at the proposed endpoint. A fresh state and decision follow this move while AP remains. Arrival does not attack, harvest or complete an objective. If selected_movement.extract_on_arrival_with_last_ap is true and this move reaches the extraction zone using the last AP, the actor extracts for zero AP after the walk; stopping short will not extract it.
distanceLevels: Minimal movement: take only the smallest legal step along the selected route.
Short movement: use about one quarter of the available distance along the selected route.
Half movement: use about half of the available distance along the selected route.
Mostly full movement: use about three quarters of the available distance along the selected route.
Full movement: use all available distance along the selected route.

gameplay.turn: This is a turn-based tactical battle: the TDF player faction acts, then the bug faction. You control only actor. A living actor with AP can act during its faction's phase; AP refreshes on its next faction turn. Enemy resources not shown are unknown.
gameplay.resources: AP means action points, HP means health points. Zero HP removes a unit. actor.ap is the budget remaining now; actor.max_ap is its normal turn budget. Each action pays its listed AP cost immediately. If AP remains, you receive an updated state and choose another action. An action marked ends_activation forfeits any AP left after paying its cost. Overwatch costs 1 AP and always ends the actor's activation.
gameplay.movement: actor.movement is movement points per AP, not remaining AP. An ordinary tile costs one movement point; infestation slows TDF and speeds bugs, and rough terrain can slow mechs. The game finds routes toward the chosen entity, objective, extraction zone, harvestable carcass, radar contact, historical sighting, map edge exit or direction using the full map layout, walls, known occupied footprints and stairs between floors. A distance question can shorten the proposed one-AP route. Every move option spends exactly one AP; unused distance cannot be saved for later.
gameplay.combat: Attack previews report hit chance in percent and damage in HP. Ranged cover and height affect shots; cover is directional and does not reduce adjacent melee damage. Armor reduces damage and armor penetration bypasses armor. Blast attacks can hurt allies and destroy cover. Profiles describe capabilities; offered previews describe the actual target.
gameplay.knowledge: Faction vision is shared. The path planner knows the full map layout through fog; unseen enemies stay unknown. capability_ref refers to shared capabilities; equipment IDs refer to equipment_definitions. Per-entity resources stay on that entity. Radar contacts are positions only; last_seen locations are historical and may be empty. Both can be investigated for sight, but are not visible attack targets. Visible carcasses can be approached by actors able to harvest them; arrival does not harvest. Objective locations are public but do not reveal hidden nest health. map_edge_exit, present only for an actor able to flee, is the edge tile it can leave the map from by the cheapest route; a fleeing unit leaves the map alive once its footprint touches any edge tile. Names in orders refer to actor.name and entities[].name.

statuses.overwatch: The unit fires at enemies that move within its weapon range during their phase, one shot per step, up to its overwatch_shots. An unfired watch lapses when its own faction's next turn begins.
statuses.hidden: Not yet revealed to the other faction. Reported only on your own faction's units; an enemy's is never shown.
statuses.suppressed: Pinned: its accuracy and movement are reduced. It holds through the unit's own next phase and clears once that phase is over.
statuses.dormant: A sleeping brood bug. It takes no actions, adds nothing to its faction's vision, and neither fires on enemies nor draws overwatch. Unless it is also burrowed it can be seen, attacked and hurt. Hurting it wakes it and its whole brood, and so does a TDF unit entering the brood's chamber, or attacking, blasting, burning or making loud noise near it.
statuses.burrowed: Under the ground. It is never spotted, attacked, blasted, burned, netted or fired on by overwatch, and it holds no tile: surface units may walk over it and stop there. It still sees from its tile, adding to its faction's vision unless it is dormant. It moves underground by tunnelling and comes up by surfacing.
statuses.fleeing: Running to escape the battle for good: the unit makes for the map edge by the cheapest route and leaves the mission once its footprint touches any edge. It never stops fleeing. Only a Broodmother flees today; her kill objective fails if she gets away.

gameplay.objectives: Each entry in objectives has a kind, described in objective_kinds. position and target_ids say where it is or which entities it concerns; they never reveal a target's hidden health. complete and failed are its recorded state: complete means achieved, failed means it can no longer be achieved. Reaching an objective's position never completes it by itself; it takes the attacks, interact actions or extraction its kind names. The interact action is offered to a TDF unit only when an objective it can work is within reach; bugs never interact. Bugs defend their nests and oppose TDF. Extraction removes the actor from this mission; use it only when its orders call for leaving. An explicit TDF extraction move reaching the zone with the last AP is followed by free extraction after the walk; other moves into the zone do not authorize extraction.

objective_kinds.destroy-spawner: Destroy an egg nest. position is the nest's tile, standing or not; visible_spawners gives its health only while it is seen. TDF destroys it with attacks, blasts, fire, or charges planted with an offered nearby interact action; merely reaching the marker does not complete it. Complete once the nest is destroyed. Bugs defend their nests.
objective_kinds.defend-generators: Hold an installation. target_ids identifies the generator entities: TDF must keep at least one alive through all waves and defeat the remaining bugs; bugs try to destroy the generators. Move toward a known generator entity to defend or attack it. Arrival does not complete a defence, interact does not work it, and failed means it has already been lost.
objective_kinds.destroy-pod: Destroy the crash site's spore pod before it matures. position is the pod's tile. TDF destroys it as it would a nest: attacks, blasts, fire, or charges planted with an offered nearby interact action. Complete once the pod is destroyed. A pod still standing when its deadline passes matures: it bursts into a wave of bugs and the objective is failed.
objective_kinds.kill-broodmother: Kill the Broodmother. While she lives, position is her tile and target_ids holds her id. TDF kills her with attacks, blasts and fire; interact does not work it. Complete when she lies dead on the map; the TDF must still extract afterwards. Failed if she escapes off a map edge, or if the mission ends or no TDF squad or mech is left on the map first. She lays a clutch of eggs every few turns and flees for a map edge once at half health or less.
objective_kinds.capture-specimen: Take a bug of the wanted species alive and bring it home. A TDF squad throws its capture net, an equipment action, over an adjacent bug of that species worn down to net.captureAtHpFraction of its maximum HP or less, then carries it (carrying names it) at reduced movement. target_ids lists the units carrying one. Complete when a carrier extracts. A carrier that dies drops its specimen: position is then where it lies, and a squad with free hands picks it up with an offered nearby interact action. Failed once no carrier, dropped specimen or net is left to bring one home.
objective_kinds.rescue-civilians: Free the civilian groups trapped in buildings and walk them to the drop ship. position is the first group still trapped; target_ids lists every civilian group still on the map, trapped or freed. A TDF squad or mech beside a trapped group frees it with an offered interact action; a freed group is a friendly civilian unit that must reach the extraction zone and extract itself. Complete once at least half the groups are aboard, and every further group aboard still counts. Failed once too many are dead for half to get out. Bugs hunt civilian groups.
objective_kinds.strip-wreck: Recover the parts of a lost mech's wreck. position is the wreck's middle tile. A TDF squad, not a mech, beside the wreck works it with an offered interact action, once per turn however many squads stand by; after enough turns of work the parts are loose. Complete once a squad that worked it extracts. Failed if the mission is lost or no squad is left that could finish it.
objective_kinds.destroy-hive-core: Bring down the hive core and get out. position is the core's middle tile; the core covers 3x3 tiles. TDF wears it down with attacks, blasts, fire, or charges planted with an offered interact action beside any face. complete is recorded the moment the core falls, but the objective is achieved only once a TDF unit has then extracted. Failed if the mission is lost. Bugs defend the core.
objective_kinds.seal-tunnels: Seal the tunnel mouths burrowers come up through. position is the next open mouth without a charge, else the next mouth not yet sealed; with no position left, every mouth is sealed. A TDF squad or mech beside an open mouth sets a charge on it with an offered interact action, and after a short fuse the mouth caves in. Once every mouth is sealed the force extracts. Failed if the mission is lost or no TDF squad or mech is left to finish it.
objective_kinds.recover-pod: Keep the spore pod alive until the recovery drop. target_ids holds the pod, a friendly entity of kind generator. When its recovery turn ends with the pod standing, the drop ship lifts it off the map and the objective is complete; the force then extracts. Failed if the pod is destroyed first. Interact does not work it. Bugs try to destroy the pod.
objective_kinds.board-core: Fight through the Spore Platform's hull and board its core. position is the hatch's middle tile, and the hatch is this stage's extraction zone: a TDF squad or mech that extracts there has boarded, and fights on in the core. Complete once one has boarded. Failed if none has boarded and none is left on the map. Interact does not work it.
objective_kinds.destroy-platform-core: Destroy the Spore Platform's core. position is the core's tile. TDF wears it down with attacks, blasts, fire, or charges planted with an offered nearby interact action. The mission is won the moment the core falls, with no extraction. The Sovereign guards it, but killing her is not required. Bugs protect the core above all.

factionGoals.tdf: Complete the mission objectives and preserve the force.
factionGoals.bugs: Defend the nests and defeat the TDF.
